band-news-bandsports.title: Grupo Bandeirantes
band-news-bandsports.shortDescription: Modernization of six Grupo Bandeirantes portals, with a shared architecture and no service interruption during migration.
band-news-bandsports.description: I led the modernization of BandSports, BandNews TV, Arte 1, Sabor & Arte, Terra Viva, and Agro+. The work combined software architecture, coordination across design and engineering, and production oversight. The scope also included content distribution through the Vivo partnership.
band-news-bandsports.challenge: Replace legacy systems while all six portals continued serving their audiences. The migration needed to balance independent delivery, consistency across teams, and traffic spikes during elections and sports events.
band-news-bandsports.solution: I defined a shared foundation in Next.js and Go, with NestJS for supporting services and independent deployments for each portal. On AWS, load balancing, WAF, gradual rollout, and automated rollback helped control the risk of each release.
band-news-bandsports.impact: All six portals moved to the new architecture without service interruption during migration. A common foundation simplified maintenance while allowing each team to evolve its portal independently.
highlights: Shared architecture with independent portal deployments
Coordination across design, frontend, backend, and infrastructure
Content distribution through the Vivo partnership

caseStudy.problem: Replace legacy systems while all six portals continued serving their audiences. The migration needed to balance independent delivery, consistency across teams, and traffic spikes during elections and sports events.
caseStudy.solution: I defined a shared foundation in Next.js and Go, with NestJS for supporting services and independent deployments for each portal. On AWS, load balancing, WAF, gradual rollout, and automated rollback helped control the risk of each release.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I owned the architecture and technical delivery. I coordinated four squads, aligned priorities and schedules with leadership, and oversaw deployments. I also worked on the code to resolve performance bottlenecks during critical migration stages.
keyDecisions: Share the technical foundation while keeping deployments independent, so standardizing components did not require migrating every portal at once.
Use Go for backend throughput and latency requirements, Next.js for the web layer, and NestJS for supporting services.
Use gradual rollout and automated rollback, making service continuity a requirement of the deployment strategy.
Use AWS for edge protection and load balancing to support changes in audience demand.
lessonsLearned: Legacy migrations require business alignment alongside technical decisions. A consistent architecture alone cannot resolve competing priorities.
Releasing in stages makes risk easier to control. The rollback plan belongs in the delivery process from the start.
results: Six portals migrated without downtime during the transition.
Shared components and lower maintenance costs for the technical foundation.
Content distribution included in the Vivo partnership.

hospital-sirio-libanes.title: Hospital Sírio-Libanês
hospital-sirio-libanes.shortDescription: Digital hospitality platform with a Go backend, Tasy integration, and an Android TV app. More than 20 million requests per month.
hospital-sirio-libanes.description: I designed and implemented the platform that delivers information and content to patient-room TVs at Hospital Sírio-Libanês. I was responsible for the backend, GCP infrastructure, and native application, integrating Tasy and playback protected by Widevine DRM.
hospital-sirio-libanes.challenge: Connect hospital-system information, protected streaming, and a TV interface in a reliable operation. The backend needed low response latency, while the application had to accommodate Android TV and the Tasy integration.
hospital-sirio-libanes.solution: I built the backend with Go and Fiber, PostgreSQL for persistence, and Redis for caching. Cloud Run provided automatic scaling without server administration. The Android TV app used Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Media3, with Widevine for content protection. Prometheus supported production monitoring.
hospital-sirio-libanes.impact: The backend served more than 20 million monthly requests, with a 6 ms average response time and a 92% cache hit rate. The platform brought hospital information and entertainment into a single experience on patient-room TVs.
highlights: Android TV application in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose
Streaming with Media3 and Widevine DRM

caseStudy.problem: Connect hospital-system information, protected streaming, and a TV interface in a reliable operation. The backend needed low response latency, while the application had to accommodate Android TV and the Tasy integration.
caseStudy.solution: I built the backend with Go and Fiber, PostgreSQL for persistence, and Redis for caching. Cloud Run provided automatic scaling without server administration. The Android TV app used Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Media3, with Widevine for content protection. Prometheus supported production monitoring.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I implemented the backend, cloud infrastructure, and Android TV app while leading the technical work. I defined the architecture, coding standards, and monitoring, and followed the integration between services and the TV experience.
keyDecisions: Use Go and Fiber to handle request volume with low backend latency.
Introduce Redis as a cache to reduce PostgreSQL access. The production cache hit rate reached 92%.
Run services on Cloud Run for automatic scaling without taking on server administration.
Integrate Media3 and Widevine in the native app to support video playback and content protection.
Include Prometheus metrics and alerts to track backend behavior in production.
lessonsLearned: Reliability depends on decisions across the entire system, from hospital-system integration to TV playback.
Production observability is part of implementation. Metrics and alerts need to evolve with the services.
Tasy integration requires clear documentation of contracts and expected behavior between systems.
results: Production backend with a 6 ms average response time.
Redis cache with a 92% hit rate, reducing database access.
Integrated Tasy, cloud services, and an Android TV app with protected content.

metricContext.averageResponse: Backend average; not the latency of the complete user experience.

fiesta-americana.title: Fiesta Americana Resort
fiesta-americana.shortDescription: International coordination of an Android TV platform that brings coaxial channels and IP streaming into one interface.
fiesta-americana.description: I led the digital hospitality project for the Fiesta Americana resort, coordinating engineering teams across countries and time zones. The delivery brought cable TV and streaming together in a native app for guest-room TVs.
fiesta-americana.challenge: Unify two content sources that previously required switching TV inputs. Beyond the application, the project depended on TV Box and USB dongle integration for the coaxial signal, with development and validation spread across international teams.
fiesta-americana.solution: I coordinated a Kotlin application with Jetpack Compose, Unicast streaming, and an electronic program guide. USB dongles and custom drivers brought the coaxial signal into the same interface. Planning aligned hardware testing cycles with software development and the teams’ time zones.
fiesta-americana.impact: The solution was deployed in the hospitality operation, bringing TV channels and streaming into the application. Guests could access both sources without switching television inputs.
highlights: Roadmap, schedules, risks, and delivery quality
Technical review of the Android TV architecture
Coaxial signal and IP streaming integration

caseStudy.problem: Unify two content sources that previously required switching TV inputs. Beyond the application, the project depended on TV Box and USB dongle integration for the coaxial signal, with development and validation spread across international teams.
caseStudy.solution: I coordinated a Kotlin application with Jetpack Compose, Unicast streaming, and an electronic program guide. USB dongles and custom drivers brought the coaxial signal into the same interface. Planning aligned hardware testing cycles with software development and the teams’ time zones.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I was responsible for project management: team alignment, the roadmap, risk tracking, and quality. My Android TV experience helped me assess architectural decisions and account for hardware constraints in delivery planning.
keyDecisions: Integrate coaxial input through USB dongles and custom drivers to make the channels available inside the application.
Use Kotlin and Jetpack Compose to bring playback and navigation into a native Android TV interface.
Plan delivery around team time zones and hardware validation cycles.
lessonsLearned: Teams in different time zones need documented decisions so work can continue without simultaneous meetings.
Hardware integration needs its own validation time. That effort must be planned alongside software development.
results: Application deployed at the resort with coaxial channels and Unicast streaming.
Program guide and navigation combined in the hospitality interface.

specialties.question: Where do I focus my technical work?
specialties.answer: I work across the full stack, with a focus on backend engineering, infrastructure, and operations. This includes Go APIs, React and Next.js applications, databases, and delivery automation on AWS and GCP.

languages.question: How do I choose languages and tools?
languages.answer: I use Go, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Kotlin, and SQL in different contexts. The choice depends on product requirements, behavior under load, team expertise, and the cost of maintaining the solution.

scale.question: What is my experience with scale and performance?
scale.answer: The documented Hospital Sírio-Libanês backend handles over 20 million requests per month, with a 6 ms average API response and a 92% cache hit rate. These measurements describe that service; the API average does not represent the latency of the entire TV experience.

fullstack.question: How do I connect frontend and backend?
fullstack.answer: I work from interfaces through API contracts, using React, Next.js, and TypeScript. Delivery includes accessibility, loading and error states, data consistency, and the performance users actually experience.

devops.question: How do I approach infrastructure and operations?
devops.answer: Build, deployment, monitoring, and recovery are part of delivery. I use CI/CD pipelines, containers, metrics, and alerts to track service behavior and investigate failures with context.

architecture.question: What guides my architecture decisions?
architecture.answer: I start with requirements and operational constraints. I define component responsibilities, model the data, and set integration limits. The team needs to understand the architecture and evolve it without turning every change into a complete migration.

responsibility.title: Who is responsible
responsibility.body: Roberto Moraes is responsible for this portfolio and the messages received through its contact channels.

contact.title: When you get in touch
contact.body: The form receives your name, email, subject, message, and optionally your company. These details are used to understand and respond to your request. Do not include passwords, financial details, health information, or other sensitive data. The site does not offer accounts, newsletters, or personalized advertising.

retention.title: Messages and retention
retention.body: The form forwards your message by email, where it becomes part of that conversation. The site does not keep a message database. Retention in the mailbox and delivery services depends on the purpose of the conversation and those services’ settings. Get in touch to request information about a message or its deletion.

services.title: Services involved
services.body: Vercel hosts the site and processes technical information needed to deliver pages and protect the service. Resend processes form delivery to the contact mailbox. These providers may process data outside Brazil. Form content is not sent to audience measurement tools.

measurement.title: Audience and performance
measurement.body: On the Vercel-hosted version, Web Analytics and Speed Insights measure visits and performance, including loading and visual stability. Page paths, referral sources, approximate location, and browser and device characteristics may be processed. These tools support statistics and site improvements; this portfolio does not configure advertising cookies or cross-site tracking.

preferences.title: Language and contact retries
preferences.body: When you select a language, the functional NEXT_LOCALE cookie may remember that choice for the browser session. It saves you from choosing the language again. You can remove it through your browser settings, which may reset your preference. The browser may also keep a random key in this tab to recognize repeated delivery attempts. It is valid for up to 24 hours, contains no form content, and is removed after delivery is confirmed.

rights.title: Requests about your data
rights.body: Use the contact email to request information, access, correction, or deletion of the data you sent. Provide enough information to locate the conversation without attaching sensitive documents. Identity confirmation may be needed to protect your data.

external.title: External links
external.body: Links to projects, social networks, and WhatsApp lead to services with their own privacy practices. Review their information before sharing data.
